A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARMA attention work, renamed WAVE in v2. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v2 do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting experiments on 12 datasets, attention-weight simulations, and diagnostic analyses, with detailed results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and simulations and reports an expanded long-horizon forecasting evaluation in Tables 5 and 11.

M1.justification: WAVE retains the forecast-length tokenization, decoder-only Transformer, token-shift residuals, indirect MA construction, activation functions, and parameter sharing of v1. The renaming and additional motivation do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The same 12 datasets and forecasting domain remain. V1's additional horizon study evaluates lengths 1 and 720 on Weather, ETTm1, and ETTm2. V2 removes length 1, adds lengths 192 and 336, and extends long-horizon coverage to Solar, ETTh1, and ETTh2.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the five attention variants and FITS, iTransformer, CATS, PatchTST, DLinear, and EncFormer. MEGA remains in its separate comparison. The expanded horizon evaluation introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: The long-horizon comparison changes from fixed baseline lookback 512 to selecting baseline results across lookbacks 512, 1024, 2048, and 4096. V2 specifies model input/output pairs (1024,96), (2048,192), (2048,336), and (4096,720), replacing v1's additional length-1/720 design. Table 11 becomes MSE-only. Appendix B.2 also revises the stated width formula to 16 times floor(sqrt(C)); the PDFs do not establish that this correction reflects rerun experiments.

E4.justification: The depth and lookback sensitivity studies, activation/sign/alpha simulations, training curves, and attention-weight case studies are retained, including appendix Tables 9–10 and Figures 7–12. V2's new Figure 2 illustrates conceptual motivation rather than adding an empirical diagnostic test.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices specify seed 2024. Neither introduces repeated-seed summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained ranking boxplots summarize different forecasting experiments rather than uncertainty across repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 5 and 11 contain a substantially expanded long-horizon result matrix and new averages. Existing 720-step entries also change: Weather linear ARMA MSE is 0.305 in v1 Table 11 and 0.295 in v2. Length-1 results and the long-horizon MAE entries disappear. Other matched result tables and empirical visualizations remain unchanged. Revised protocols limit interpretation of the changed scores as fixed-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the attention definitions, residual-to-MA transformation, inverse relationship between B and Theta, and simplified lag-decay derivation. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption appears in the appendices; the added motivation is conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of competitive decoder-only forecasting, efficient MA integration, temporal-effect decoupling, and state-of-the-art performance. WAVE renames the contribution without substantively changing these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 2.5 contrasts persistent seasonal effects in forecasting with NLP dependencies to explain why exponential decay can be unsuitable. V2 also removes v1's explicit explanation that lookback 512 with horizon 720 collapses tokenization to a single-token MLP. The inter-series limitation and proposed future applications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 explicitly rounds down sqrt(C) in the hidden-width formula. The abstract's code hyperlink changes from a named GitHub repository to an anonymous.4open.science mirror; availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Other implementation, hardware, optimizer, and training-budget disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against gated/EMA attention, previous neural ARMA models, and forecasting architectures remain. Related work moves from v1 Section 4 to v2 Appendix B, with bibliographic formatting changes.

P1.justification: V2 renames the paper and method, adds a motivation subsection, tokenization footnote, and Impact Statement, moves related work to the appendix, and reorganizes the forecasting discussion into short- and long-horizon results. Most technical prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two columns. V1 Figures 1–2 are merged into v2 Figure 1, a new explanatory Figure 2 appears, and colored performance tables become unshaded tables. Depth/lookback Tables 3–4 exchange numbers, Figure 6 and Table 7 move to the appendix, and Tables 5/11 are redesigned for the revised evaluation.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens long-horizon evidence and clarifies the motivation, but reporting inconsistencies affect its principal added validation. Table 5 specifies lookback 1024 for horizon 96, while Table 11 repeats the lookback-512 model scores from Table 8 and conflicts with Table 10's lookback-1024 results, such as Weather linear ARMA MSE 0.139 versus 0.141. Table 11 also promises MAE but reports only MSE. These unresolved issues prevent confidently weighing the expanded validation against reduced reporting reliability.
